subject: Re: Clock drift at west-edge causing partial degradation — request to recalc uptime
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@bluestream.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeFlow Support <support@edgeflow.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clock drift at west-edge causing 40m partial degradation — request uptime recalculation

Hi Vanessa / Neha,

Quick note from BlueStream ops. On 2026-04-30 between ~02:18 and 02:58 UTC (our telemetry), a subset of west-edge nodes experienced an NTP/clock drift resulting in mis-aligned timestamps and health-check flapping. This manifested as short-lived 5xx spikes and persistent error counts for routed L7 traffic — roughly a 40 minute window of partial degradation for customers routed through that POP.

We're attaching the logs (edge-drift-log-20260430.txt) and a report from our provider (EdgeFlow). From our perspective this was caused by their maintained router cluster failing to sync time after a control-plane failover; traffic was not fully blackholed but there was increased error surface until a manual reroute at 03:02 UTC.

Can Redwood please:
- Recalculate BlueStream's uptime percentage for April using the SLO definition in our contract (section 3.1) with an exclusion for third-party time-synced outages if applicable;
- Confirm whether the incident should be considered a third-party outage or under Redwood responsibility;
- Let us know any data you need (I've attached logs and can share more raw syslogs on request).

Thanks — we appreciate a timely response since this touches renewal/credits.

— Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Ops, BlueStream
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@bluestream.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Clock drift at west-edge causing 40m partial degradation — request uptime recalculation

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for sending the logs. I took an initial pass. A couple of questions to help us determine credit eligibility:

1) Contract SLO reference — can you confirm the exact SLO window you want us to recalc against? Our default for BlueStream is monthly uptime measured at 1-minute granularity (section 3.1 as you noted) but I want to be explicit about the calculation start/end boundaries.
2) You mention a manual reroute at 03:02 UTC — our internal events show a health-check spike that persisted until ~03:05 UTC. Is the 03:02 UTC timestamp the moment EdgeFlow triggered the reroute or when BlueStream changed routing on your side?
3) Please confirm whether EdgeFlow's bulletin includes an admission of responsibility for the clock sync issue (their case number is helpful).

We'll need:
- the raw syslog snippets for the affected POPs (if you can paste or share a short export),
- EdgeFlow's incident note (if different from the attached), and
- any customer-visible reroute timestamps from your LB.

Cc-ing Ben to keep Sales in the loop since credits/renewal may be impacted. I'll route to Marissa in CS when we have the final timeline so we can propose a credit if applicable.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference
From: EdgeFlow Support <support@edgeflow.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah@bluestream.io>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 02:21:09 +0000
Subject: Re: Clock drift at west-edge causing 40m partial degradation — request uptime recalculation

Hi all,

Thanks for flagging. EdgeFlow engineering confirms that one router cluster in the us-west POP experienced a control-plane failover which temporarily prevented NTP daemons from re-syncing (case EF-992). Impact window per our control-plane is 2026-04-30T02:14:00Z to 2026-04-30T03:06:00Z; root cause was a firmware mismatch combined with a transient NTP server outage upstream.

We observed increasing health-check timeouts and automatic service restarts; traffic was not blackholed but there were transient 5xx responses and connection resets for some sessions until the cluster was back to steady-state at ~03:06Z. We are attaching the provider diagnostic excerpt and a short CSV of per-node error counts (edge-drift-log-20260430.txt).

Case EF-992: https://edgeflow.inc/cases/EF-992 (internal link)

EdgeFlow's position: this is a third-party infrastructure incident stemming from their control-plane; they have offered to share their incident postmortem and collaborate on timestamps if you need us to pull further telemetry.

Regards,
EdgeFlow Support
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah@bluestream.io>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:14:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Clock drift at west-edge causing 40m partial degradation — request uptime recalculation

Looping commercial perspective in.

Thanks for the quick investigation so far — looks like three inputs matter: raw timestamps (EdgeFlow), our per-request success-rate logs, and BlueStream's routing cutover time. From a renewal/credit standpoint I'd propose we:

- Accept a remediation credit proportional to the validated user-impact window (if EdgeFlow's timeline and our logs align).
- If the exact window is ambiguous we split the difference and provide a one-off prorated credit for the affected minutes rather than a full monthly SLA breach credit (keeps precedent reasonable).

If ops/legal want to push harder on full credit we can, but given this appears to be an upstream control-plane issue, a proportional credit is standard. Recommend Marissa take point on the customer comms and Ben/Finance will prep the credit calc once Neha confirms the final window.

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@bluestream.io>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clock drift at west-edge causing 40m partial degradation — request uptime recalculation

Thanks everyone — finalizing the decision after reviewing the attached spreadsheet (slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx) and cross-checking our ingestion pipeline logs. Summary:

- EdgeFlow's incident window: 2026-04-30T02:14:00Z - 2026-04-30T03:06:00Z (EdgeFlow).
- BlueStream reports manual reroute at 2026-04-30T03:02:00Z (BlueStream).
- Our ingress traces show elevated 5xx counts from 02:17Z to 03:05Z; the majority of customer-facing errors cluster 02:18Z-02:58Z (consistent with Sarah's claim).

Decision: We will treat this as a third-party provider incident for the purposes of SLA apportionment but will provide BlueStream a one-off prorated credit representing the customer-visible partial degradation window (02:18Z-02:58Z = 40 minutes). This aligns with Ben's recommendation to avoid setting broad precedent while making the customer whole for measurable impact.

Action items:
- Neha: please confirm the final minute-level calc and push the credit task to Finance (reference HubSpot ticket HS-4532).
- Ben: prepare the credit memo; Marissa will draft the customer-facing note.
- Vanessa: include the attachments and EdgeFlow's case EF-992 link in the customer comms.

I've uploaded the SLO calc and the minute-by-minute logs to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-share-link/slo-recalc. Attaching the SLO workbook for records (slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx).

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
